title: Magnetic flux
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:41Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches the general form Φ = BA cos θ with the angle to the normal and asks a question that needs cos θ, while the new point is the narrower right-angle form Φ = BA, so it is a broader card and needs new content rather than small changes.

draft.title: Magnetic flux
card: Magnetic flux measures how much magnetic field passes through a surface. For a field at right angles to the surface, Φ = BA.
B is the magnetic field strength in tesla (T) and A is the area in square metres (m²). Flux is measured in weber (Wb), where 1 Wb = 1 T m².
Only the part of the field at right angles to the surface counts. If the field runs along the surface, no field lines pass through it and the flux is zero.
Flux rises if the field gets stronger or the area gets larger. Tilting a coil changes how much field passes through it, so the flux changes too.
draft.remember: Flux is field times area, counted at right angles to the surface.

a.q: A square coil of area 0.020 m² sits at right angles to a uniform field of 0.50 T. What is the magnetic flux through it?
a.why: Φ = BA = 0.50 × 0.020 = 0.010 Wb. Dividing B by A gives 25, which is the wrong operation, because flux is the product of the two.

b.q: Priya holds a flat loop in a steady magnetic field so that the field lines pass straight through it. She then turns the loop until its flat face is parallel to the field lines. What happens to the flux through the loop?
b.why: Only the part of the field at right angles to the surface counts. When the face is parallel to the field, no field lines pass through it, so the flux is zero. The field and the area have not changed, but that does not keep the flux the same.
b.clue: Do any field lines pass through the loop once it lies along them?
